approved: Social Security Amendment (Supporting More Australians into Work) Bill 2013
Social Security Amendment (Supporting More Australians into Work) Bill 2013 - Second Reading - Increase Newstart and support single parents

Introduced a bill letting unemployed Australians and single parents on income support earn $100 a fortnight, $38 more than currently allowed, before payments reduce, investing $258 million over four years, and said from 20 March 2014 affected recipients could see an average increase of about $494 a year.

Argued that the bill responds inadequately to the impact of moving single parents from Parenting Payment to Newstart, while proposing an increase in the income-free area from $62 to $100, education assistance and a 12-week concession-card extension.
Argued that Labor and the coalition had jointly harmed single parents, citing reduced payments, housing pressures and inadequate Newstart support, while supporting the bill as a partial improvement.

Argued that moving single parents onto Newstart unfairly harmed vulnerable families, especially in regional areas, and said the bill offered limited assistance while calling for the changes to be repealed.
Announced that the bill would increase the income-free area to $100 per fortnight, extend education assistance and preserve the pensioner concession card for 12 weeks for eligible single parents.

Two reports were tabled: one on the Social Security Amendment (Supporting More Australians into Work) Bill 2013 and one on the Early Years Quality Fund Special Account Bill 2013, both ordered to be printed.

The bill increases the income-free area for Newstart and other allowances from $62 to $100 per fortnight, extends the pensioner education supplement to single parents on Newstart, and provides a 12‑week extension of the pensioner concession card for single parents leaving parenting payment. The opposition and the Greens supported the bill but criticised it as insufficient, with the Greens calling for a $50‑per‑week increase to Newstart and additional support for single parents.
